verdict.rationale: Gram lets users register third-party or custom remote MCP servers as sources. It verifies each one with an MCP initialize probe, proxies it behind a governed endpoint, imports official servers from the MCP Registry, and supports tunneled servers. Its in-dashboard agent harness then chats with a model that calls those servers' tools. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration (all evidence is vendor docs); the product's own agentic use of plugged-in tools is limited to a testing harness, with the main purpose being to proxy them to external clients.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Registering the server as a remote source closes that gap. The Control Plane creates an endpoint that proxies the upstream, and the team connects to that endpoint instead.
Verify probes the URL with an MCP initialize request and confirms the endpoint is reachable and speaking the protocol before the server is created.
Every tool source in the project in one place: OpenAPI documents, TypeScript functions, third-party catalog servers, custom remote MCP servers, and tunneled MCP servers.
Discover and import official third-party MCP servers, powered by the official MCP Registry.
pick a server, authenticate, chat with a model that calls the tools, and inspect the logs.
